sections.html:
Altoona is a railroad city of about 42,300 people in Blair County, built on hillsides in the Allegheny Mountains. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 42,347 residents, down 3.6 percent from the 2020 base. Population peaked at 82,054 in the 1930 census and has dropped in every count since.

Prices sit far below the national level: an owner-occupied home has a median value of $119,900, while the figure for the United States is $332,700. About 63.9 percent of occupied homes are owned. Median gross rent is $819, and median household income is $51,250. At that price level, a repair bill can eat a large share of what the house will sell for. Get a firm estimate before deciding how to sell.

The Pennsylvania Railroad founded Altoona in 1849 as a shop and maintenance site, and the housing followed the work. Many older districts mix rowhouses with single homes built for workers and managers. The manager houses are narrow and tall, resemble Victorian or Edwardian mansions, and have often been converted to double or triple family apartments.

Rowhouses share walls and rooflines between units, so a roof or drainage problem next door can affect you. Streets are numbered: Streets run northwest to southeast, and Avenues run northeast to southwest. The hillsides, the cold winters and about 136 days of precipitation a year put steady wear on roofs, gutters and basements, and buyers know it.

Learn the right section name before you write a listing.

  • Downtown and Center City: the Downtown Altoona Historic District, with multistory brick buildings from around 1900.
  • Main sections: Logantown, Fairview, Juniata, Wehnwood, Calvert Hills, the 5th and 6th Wards, Westmont, Eldorado, East End, Dutch Hill, Pleasant Valley, Hileman Heights, Mansion Park, Llyswen, Garden Heights and Highland Park.
  • Named neighborhoods: Little Italy, Gospel Hill, Toy Town, Columbia Park, Knickerbockers and Curtin.
  • Outside the city: Lakemont, Greenwood, Bellmeade and Newburg are treated as parts of Altoona but lie in Logan Township.

Logan Township wraps around the city, and a parcel's tax bill and codes office both depend on which side of the boundary it is on. For a parcel check, use the floodplain information page and the zoning and GIS map on the city website.

Anyone who buys or sells in Altoona owes real estate transfer tax, and the Blair County Recorder of Deeds collects it. The rate adds up to 2 percent: the state takes 1 percent, and the other 1 percent is divided between the city and the Altoona Area School District.

The Blair County Assessment Office is at 423 Allegheny Street, Suite 041, Hollidaysburg, phone 814-693-3110. Request the appeal form and the yearly filing deadline there. Your closing agent can explain how the transfer tax is divided.

Every owner of a leased or non-owner-occupied dwelling in Altoona must hold a Conditional Housing Permit, which becomes a Residential Rental Unit License after the unit passes inspection. Licenses are renewed on or before July 31 each year, and most units are inspected every three years.

  • An inspection takes 20 to 30 minutes, and the owner, tenant or a representative must be present.
  • Inspectors use the International Property Maintenance Code on the interior and exterior.
  • Owners usually get 45 days to repair violations, with extensions in 30-day steps, and life-safety hazards must be corrected immediately.
  • Heat must be supplied from October 1 to May 15, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are checked.

Landlords should confirm license status with Codes and Inspections at 1301 12th Street, Suite 103, phone 814-949-2456, and ask whether any inspection applies to the property at sale. Hand the buyer a copy of the license and the latest inspection result if you have them.

sections.h2: Vacant houses and open code notices
sections.html:
With an empty house, ask Codes and Inspections whether a property maintenance notice is open before you list. Such a notice stays with the building, and the buyer's title company will probably turn it up. Mowing the yard, boarding a broken window or correcting the violation now usually costs less than haggling over it at settlement. Gather the deed, the tax bills from H. A. Berkheimer and the county, and any permit records, before the first showing.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a house fast
sections.html:
Owners here have three routes. Listing with an agent reaches the widest audience but means open houses, an inspection by the buyer and a lender's timetable. Selling privately keeps the commission and puts the paperwork on you. A cash offer closes fastest and with the least doubt, though the price reflects repairs the buyer absorbs.

Before choosing, get a rough repair estimate and ask a few buyers for written offers. Compare what each one would leave you after payoffs and transfer tax, and ask when each could close.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Altoona
sections.html:
Paperwork comes first. The title company needs the deed and searches for liens, unpaid taxes and open notices. Get current balances from Blair County and H. A. Berkheimer, because either can appear on the settlement statement. When a mortgage is open, ask the lender for a payoff figure.

Next, decide who pays the 2 percent transfer tax. The sales agreement sets that, and it is one of the easiest items to bargain over. For a rental, add the license check with Codes and Inspections and a copy of any lease the buyer will inherit.

You sign the deed and settlement papers at closing, and the transfer is recorded in the Blair County Recorder of Deeds office. In a cash sale no lender appraisal or underwriting is involved, which leaves title work and your move-out date. Cash buyers can therefore often commit to a quick closing, useful for an inherited house, a vacant property or a move that cannot wait.

Health care leads local employment, with UPMC Altoona and the James E. Van Zandt VA Medical Center. Penn State Altoona has a downtown presence. I-99 and US 22 link the city to the wider region, and a single school district, the Altoona Area School District, covers the whole city.

faqs.q: Does Altoona have a transfer tax when I sell my house?
faqs.a: Yes. It is 2 percent in total: 1 percent to the state and 1 percent shared by the city and the school district. The Blair County Recorder of Deeds collects it.

faqs.q: When must Altoona landlords renew their rental license?
faqs.a: On or before July 31 each year. Most units are inspected every three years, and owners generally get 45 days to fix violations found.

faqs.q: Who collects real estate tax on an Altoona home?
faqs.a: H. A. Berkheimer collects the city's local real estate tax, at 7.129 mils. Blair County and the school district bill separately.

faqs.q: Is Lakemont inside the city of Altoona?
faqs.a: No. Lakemont, Greenwood, Bellmeade and Newburg are treated as parts of Altoona but lie in Logan Township, outside city limits.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about assessment changes in Blair County?
faqs.a: Call the Blair County Assessment Office in Hollidaysburg at 814-693-3110. It handles appeal forms and can tell you the filing deadline for the year.
